RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday,  the December 19, 2008/Agrahayana 28, 1930 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Agriculture; Chemicals and Fertilizers; Consumer Affairs, Food
and Public Distribution; Health and Family Welfare; Micro, Small and
Medium Enterprises; Railways; Steel)
Total number of questions — 20
89
Optimum use of raw materials
*261. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased
to state:
(a) whether experts on steel feel that
every ounce of raw materials, such as iron-
ore, coal and manganese whose prices are
touching all time high, should be used
properly;
(b) if so, whether utilisation of every
ounce of these raw materials is of
fundamental importance as they play a very
important role in the strategy of a company;
(c) whether steel companies have been
urged to make optimum use of raw materials
so that steel industry works well;
(d) if so, to what extent efforts in this
regard have been taken by them; and
(e) to what extent results have been
achieved?
Admission of SC/ST students in
medical colleges
*262. SHRI A. VIJAY ARAGHAV AN:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether competent authority is
aware that many students of Scheduled
Caste and Scheduled Tribe catagory are
deprived of admission to M.B.B.S. course
in various medical colleges since they did
not receive qualifying marks prescribed by
the Medical Council of India (MCI) for
entrance examination;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is a fact that many seats
are not filled with SC/ST candidates due to
the above instruction of MCI;
(d) if so, whether steps will be taken to
fill the seats considering the marks received
in the qualifying examination and the
entrance examination as parameters; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?

90
Ship breaking at Alang
*263. SHRIMATI JAYA BACHCHAN:
Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a ship 'SS
Oceanic' carrying 250 tonnes of asbestos, a
toxic material, was headed for Alang in
Saurashtra coast;
(b) whether it is a fact that Alang Ship
Breaking Yard has earned infamy because
of its poor handling of toxic waste from
dismantled ships; and
(c) if so, the steps Government has
taken on both the counts?
Heavy metals in ayurvedic medicines
*264. DR. JANARDHAN
WAGHMARE:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the American drug regulator,
Food and Drug Administration (FDA), has
recently revised and issued its import alert
following recent findings that ayurvedic
drugs shipped from India contained high
level of toxic heavy metals;
(b) if so, the facts thereof and the details
of the companies and names of the
ayurvedic drugs to which Government have
allowed export and were found to contain
detectable levels of heavy metals; and
(c) the steps Government proposes to
take to ban manufacture/sale/export of such
ayurvedic drugs which contain toxic heavy
metals?
Disbursement of funds by NAFED to
private parties
*265. SHRI S.S. AHLUWALIA: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the National Agriculture
Cooperative Marketing Federation
(NAFED) has disbursed huge funds to
private parties under the pretext of
promoting exports of even non-agricultural
items like iron-ore;
(b) if so, the volume of funds so given
to private parties indicating details of
identities of recipient private parties, along
with dates of disbursal to respective parties
and the terms thereof;
(c) whether these parties have largely
defaulted in repaying the funds as per the
terms;
(d) if so, the details thereof, indicating
its impact on the financial health of NAFED;
and
(e) the steps taken, if any, for recovery
of the outstanding dues from those parties?
Pregnancy related deaths
*266. SHRI B.J. PANDA:
MS. MABEL REBELLO:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
half a million of women die during child-
birth, of whom 70,000 are from India, in
other words a women dies every six minutes
from a pregnancy-related cause in India, as
per a new survey conducted by an NGO
"The White Ribbon Alliance India";
(b) whether Government is also aware
that a country's maternal mortality rate is
considered to be the best indicator of its
health system; and

91
(c) if so, what is the action plan of
Government to control the high rate of
women mortality during child-birth?
Supply of foodgrains to ration card
holders
*267. SHRI VIJAYKUMAR RUPANI:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) the criteria set for determining Below
Poverty Line (BPL);
(b) the steps taken by Government so
that the ration cards are only issued to
genuine house-holds; and
(c) the steps taken for the storage of
foodgrains to ensure regular and adequate
supply to ration card holders?
Prices of food items
†*268. SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a growth rate
of 9.3 per cent was registered in the prices
of food items in the week ending November
8, 2008, while the Common Wholesale Price
Index rate was estimated to be less than the
above rate;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the
increase in prices of food items in the
country creates a formidable financial crisis
for the common man of the country; and
(d) if so, the reaction of Government
thereto?
Implementation of National Policy for
Farmers
*269. PROF. M.S. SW AMINATHAN:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether he placed a National Policy
for Farmers on the Table of the House in
November, 2007;
(b) if so, the action taken so far to
implement this policy; and
(c) what steps have been taken to attract
and retain youth in farming being one of
the objectives of the Policy?
Protection of foodgrains from pests
*270. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: W ill the Minister of
CONSUMER  AFFAIRS, FOOD AND
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government is aware that
pests eat away foodgrains worth several
crores every year;
(b) if so, whether any exact assessment
in this regard has been made;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether to protect foodgrains from
pests, Government has formulated any
strategy to bring in the use of pesticides
without hurting environment and human
health; and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Terrorist attacks and security
arrangements on railway
stations
*271. SHRI KAMAL AKHTAR: Will
the Minister of RAILW AYS be pleased to
state:
(a) the details and the number of people
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

92
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
killed and injured at CST railway station in
Mumbai during the recent terrorist attack;
(b) whether a bomb blast took place in
Tinsukia train at Difu station on 2nd
December, 2008;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether railway stations and trains
are not fully safe and security arrangements
there are not satisfactory; and
(e) if so, the details thereof and the
concrete measures Government proposes
to take to make Railways' security
foolproof along with the earlier measures
taken and fresh initiatives taken after these
terrorist attacks?
Oil pilferage from trains
*272. SHRI AMIR ALAM KHAN:
Will the Minister of  RAILW AYS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether large quantity of petrol/
diesel is being pilfered from trains during
their transit with the collusion of employees
of petroleum companies and the Railways;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the number of cases of oil pilferage
reported during the last year and the current
year; and
(d) the action taken by Government
against those employees found involved in
oil pilferage or caught red-handed in each
of such cases?
Damage to foodgrains
†*273. SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to refer to
the reply to Starred Question 104 given in
the Rajya Sabha on the 24th October, 2008
and state:
(a) the time when his Ministry received
information regarding damage to foodgrains
amounting to 846 lakh tonnes in 2005-06,
726 lakh tonnes in 2006-07, 750 lakh
tonnes in 2007-08 and 452 lakh tonnes till
September, 2008 in 2008-09;
(b) the time when the above foodgrains
were procured, the amount spent on its
maintenance and the places where it was
kept;
(c) the market price of damaged
foodgrains, the amount spent on disposing
of the same and the reasons for rotting of
foodgrains at each place; and
(d) the officers held responsible for
that?
Ban on use of tobacco
*274. SHRI JAI PRAKASH
NARAYAN SINGH: Will the Minister of
HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether smokers emit cancerous
smoke and pollute air;
(b) if so, the details of measures taken
to eliminate smoking; and
(c) whether there is any proposal to
ban use of tobacco in all forms?
Shortage of quality seeds
*275. SHRI T.T.V . DHINAKARAN:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there is a severe shortage of
seeds, particularly quality seeds in the
country;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and

93
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(c) the action taken to ensure the
availability  of quality seeds?
Requirement of iron-ore by steel
companies
*276. SHRI N.R. GOVINDARAJAR:
Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased to
state:
(a) how much iron-ore is required by all
steel companies in Jharkhand for expansion/
Greenfield projects;
(b) whether it is a fact that Steel
Authority of India Limited (SAIL) would
require nearly 800 million tonnes of ore for
the next 30 years;
(c) if so, whether expansion plans of
SAIL would be taken into account and if
not, the reasons therefor; and
(d) how Government has come to the
conclusion that 800 million tonnes are
enough for SAIL to meet its expansion
plans?
Revival of closed fertilizer units
†*277. SHRI RUDRA NARAYAN
PANY: Will the Minister of CHEMICALS
AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has taken any
concrete steps for revival of fertilizer
factories operated by the Fertilizer
Corporation of  India (FCI), the Hindustan
Fertilizer Corporation (HFC), etc. which
are now lying closed;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Gauge conversion in the NER
*278. SHRI BISWAJIT DAIMARY:
Will the Minister of RAILWA YS be pleased
to state:
(a) whether railway lines from Rangia
to Murkongsilec (Jonai) and Guwahati to
Cachar are being upgraded from  metre-
gauge to broad-gauge;
(b) if so, the schedule of their
completion;
(c) if not, the reasons for delay;
(d) whether in Agartala, Railways have
taken up a metre-gauge line recently instead
of a broad-gauge line;
(e) if so, the details thereof and the
reasons for not providing broad-gauge line
instead;
(f) whether there is any provision to
extend railway line to Meghalaya, Mizoram
and Manipur which are having tourist
potential;
(g) if so, the details thereof; and
(h) if not, the reasons therefor?
Procurement of anti-rabbies vaccine
*279. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Central Government
hospitals in the Capital are procuring poor
quality anti-rabbies vaccine for patients;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that most
developed nations have discontinued the
use of equine serum, being outdated; and
(d) if so, the reasons of continuing
outdated treatment of patients bitten by
dogs?

94
Effect of economic recession on
Railways
†*280. SHRI PRABHA T JHA: Will the
Minister of RAILW AYS be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Railways
have also been affected by the economic
recession, which has pervaded almost all
the sectors in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that freightage
has been adversely affected due to this;
and
(d) if so, the details thereof for the last
one year?
N
EW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 13th December, 2008 Secretary-General.
Agrahayana 22, 1930 (Saka)
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

I N D E X
(Ministry-wise)
Agriculture : 265, 269, 275,
Chemicals and Fertilizers : 277,

Public Distribution : 267, 268, 270, 273,
